html:
Incwala is the most sacred ceremony of the Swazi, a kingship ritual held each year around the summer solstice in December and January, in which the king is renewed and the first fruits of the harvest are tasted.

Messengers fetch water from the sea and rivers, young men cut sacred branches, and regiments sing songs that may be heard only at this time. The king is secluded and then dances before the nation, eating the new crops first.

It grew strong under Mswati II and survived colonial rule and missionary opposition. It remains central to the monarchy's claim to embody the nation, alongside the reed dance. Its survival is one reason Eswatini keeps its absolute monarchy.
sum: Incwala is the most sacred ceremony of the Swazi, a kingship ritual held each year around the summer solstice in December and January, in which the king is renewed and the first fruits of the harvest are tasted.
